content: 1. A higher or lower concentration of a specific substance in serum, blood, urine, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), or other bodily fluids can be diagnostic of a particular condition. 2. Laboratory findings that align with the diagnosis of a specific condition may include specific abnormalities, such as elevated or reduced levels of certain markers. 3. In patients with certain conditions, laboratory values are typically within normal ranges. 4. Some individuals with a specific condition may exhibit elevated or reduced concentrations of a particular substance, which is often indicative of the condition or its underlying pathology. 5. There are no specific laboratory findings that are diagnostic of certain conditions. 6. Laboratory findings consistent with the diagnosis of a particular condition may include specific patterns or abnormalities in test results. 7. In some cases, patients with a specific condition may demonstrate abnormal levels of a particular substance, which can provide a clue to the diagnosis or suggest the presence of the condition.
